manifest.name: Payment Provider: Buckaroo
manifest.summary: A Dutch payment provider covering several countries in Europe.
manifest.author: Odoo S.A.

models._description: Payment Provider (Buckaroo credentials: website key / secret key)
Payment Transaction (Buckaroo BPE hosted-redirect HTML gateway flow; no direct API, no tokenization)
relations: no new fields; 4 methods overriding payment's rendering/notification hooks

security.note: No own ACL/rules; relies on payment's security and on the base.group_system field group guarding buckaroo_secret_key (the website key is left ungrouped).

views.note: xml_loc=47: payment.provider form inheritance (payment_provider_views.xml: Buckaroo website key + secret key, shown only when code=='buckaroo', secret key password-masked) + the QWeb redirect-form template payment_buckaroo_templates.xml (auto-submit POST form to the Buckaroo HTML gateway with Brq_websitekey/Brq_amount/Brq_currency/Brq_invoicenumber/Brq_signature[/Brq_culture]/Brq_return/Brq_returncancel/Brq_returnerror/Brq_returnreject), plus data/payment_provider_data.xml wiring redirect_form_view_id. No own model views.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._get_specific_rendering_values -> hidden-field POST redirect to the Buckaroo BPE HTML gateway (https://checkout.buckaroo.nl/html/ ; sandbox https://testcheckout.buckaroo.nl/html/)
behavioral_notes.observation: Buckaroo is a pure hosted-redirect acquirer: there is NO server-to-server payment API call. _get_specific_rendering_values builds the BPE gateway payload (Brq_websitekey=buckaroo_website_key, Brq_amount=tx.amount, Brq_currency=currency.name, Brq_invoicenumber=tx.reference, and ALL FOUR result URLs Brq_return/Brq_returncancel/Brq_returnerror/Brq_returnreject set to the same base_url+/payment/buckaroo/return -- they are included separately because each participates in the signature; plus Brq_culture=partner_lang with '_'->'-' when a partner lang is set). It then signs the dict via provider._buckaroo_generate_digital_sign(rendering_values, incoming=False) into Brq_signature and adds api_url=provider._buckaroo_get_api_url() (live checkout.buckaroo.nl vs sandbox testcheckout.buckaroo.nl by provider.state). These values feed the redirect_form QWeb template whose hidden inputs auto-POST the browser to Buckaroo's hosted HTML gateway. The acquirer endpoint and the signed-form handoff are invisible to Python model/field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.provider._buckaroo_generate_digital_sign -> SHA-1 signing over prefix-filtered, lowercase-sorted key=value pairs + shared secret
behavioral_notes.observation: _buckaroo_generate_digital_sign implements Buckaroo's BPE scheme: it keeps ONLY items whose key (case-insensitively) starts with 'add_', 'brq_' or 'cust_'; for INCOMING data it first URL-decodes each value (urls.url_unquote_plus) and EXCLUDES the 'brq_signature' key itself; it sorts the surviving pairs by lower-cased key (the comment notes lower-case is required because ord('A') < ord('_') < ord('a')); concatenates them as 'key=value' (empty value -> '') with no separator; appends buckaroo_secret_key; and returns hashlib.sha1(sign_string.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest(). The digest is fixed at SHA-1 (not configurable, not an HMAC) and the same routine serves both directions via the incoming flag (outgoing skips the URL-decode/exclusion). This prefix-filtered, lowercase-sorted, secret-appended SHA-1 is pure code semantics, not derivable from metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: BuckarooController.buckaroo_return_from_checkout (/payment/buckaroo/return, POST) + buckaroo_webhook (/payment/buckaroo/webhook, POST) -> _normalize_data_keys + _verify_signature(incoming) BEFORE _process; reference via _extract_reference -> brq_invoicenumber
behavioral_notes.observation: Both public, csrf=False POST routes share the same guarded pattern. Each first calls _normalize_data_keys (lower-cases every key, since Buckaroo param names are case-insensitive), extracts received_signature=data['brq_signature'], then _search_by_reference('buckaroo', data) (via _extract_reference -> data['brq_invoicenumber']) locates the tx. _verify_signature is called BEFORE _process and, on the RAW (un-normalized) data, recomputes the signature with incoming=True; it rejects with werkzeug Forbidden (HTTP 403) when received_signature is missing or when hmac.compare_digest(received, expected) fails -- a constant-time compare. The return route additionally carries save_session=False (so a SameSite-less session cookie is not lost on the cross-site POST) and redirects to /payment/status; the webhook returns '' to acknowledge. Both then call tx_sudo._process('buckaroo', normalized data), which validates the amount (via _extract_amount_data) then runs _apply_updates. Both routes are thus authenticated and authoritative -- Buckaroo needs no separate verification GET.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._apply_updates -> Buckaroo BRQ_STATUSCODE -> payment state mapping
behavioral_notes.observation: _apply_updates reads brq_transactions, which may be a comma-separated list of Buckaroo transaction keys; it sets provider_reference to the FIRST key (split(',')[0]) and _set_error's ('missing transaction keys') if absent. It resolves the payment method from brq_payment_method via payment.method._get_from_code(..., mapping=const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING) (falling back to the current method), then maps int(brq_statuscode) through const.STATUS_CODES_MAPPING into payment's guarded transitions: 790/791/792/793 -> _set_pending; 190 -> _set_done; 890/891 -> _set_canceled; 690 -> _set_error('payment refused'); 490/491/492 -> _set_error('error during processing'); any other code -> _set_error('Unknown status code'). _extract_amount_data reads brq_amount and brq_currency for the engine's amount cross-check. This inbound numeric-status->state translation (including the distinct refused vs error vs cancel buckets) is pure code, not visible in metadata.

_get_supported_currencies overrides payment to filter the engine's currencies down to const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES for code=='buckaroo' -- exactly EUR, GBP, PLN, DKK, NOK, SEK, CHF, USD (the eight Buckaroo supports). _get_default_payment_method_codes returns const.DEFAULT_PAYMENT_METHOD_CODES (card + ideal + visa/mastercard/amex/discover) when Buckaroo is activated; note const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING maps the generic 'card' code to Buckaroo's 'mastercard' service and covers European methods (iDEAL, Bancontact, Belfius, KBC, SOFORT, Przelewy24, EPS, Trustly, Klarna, in3/Capayable, SEPA Direct Debit, ...). This currency bounding + method mapping is enforced in code, not visible as plain field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration surface (gap #7) -- endpoints, secret key (no transport API key)
behavioral_notes.observation: Static gap-#7 facts (extract_frontend.py): uses_api_keys=true (because of the pre-shared buckaroo_secret_key), but there is NO outbound REST client: the only declared endpoints are the Buckaroo BPE HTML gateways -- https://checkout.buckaroo.nl/html/ (live) and https://testcheckout.buckaroo.nl/html/ (sandbox) -- selected by provider.state in models/payment_provider.py (_buckaroo_get_api_url). Buckaroo is reached purely by the browser POSTing the signed hidden-field form to the HTML gateway, and Buckaroo returns to Odoo's /payment/buckaroo/return + pushes to /payment/buckaroo/webhook. The 'API key' is the pre-shared secret used ONLY to compute/verify the SHA-1 signature (buckaroo_secret_key), not a bearer token on any HTTP call -- so unlike Stripe/Xendit there is no authenticated S2S endpoint here. This redirect-only acquirer link is the canonical metadata gap #7.

0 JS files, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 0 patches (gap #3). payment_buckaroo ships no client-side code: the entire buyer interaction is the server-rendered redirect_form QWeb template (payment_buckaroo_templates.xml) whose hidden inputs auto-submit to the Buckaroo HTML gateway. There is no browser SDK and no inline card form -- card/iDEAL/wallet data are collected on Buckaroo's hosted page, never in Odoo. The only browser-visible artifact is the auto-POST redirect form (plain server-rendered HTML, no gap-#3 JS surface).

it_architecture.application: payment_buckaroo (Buckaroo acquirer adapter for the payment engine; _inherit-only, no own models/views)
software_services: /payment/buckaroo/return (redirect-return, http POST, csrf=False, save_session=False: signature-verified, processes, then /payment/status)
/payment/buckaroo/webhook (async push notification, http POST, csrf=False: signature-verified, processes, returns '')
data_objects: payment.transaction (Buckaroo BPE hosted-redirect HTML gateway flow; no new fields; 4 override methods)
logical_data_erm: payment.transaction -> payment.provider (provider_id; provider_code=='buckaroo' gates every override)
external: payment.transaction.reference == Buckaroo Brq_invoicenumber/brq_invoicenumber (cross-system key for return/webhook lookup via _extract_reference)
external: payment.transaction.provider_reference == Buckaroo transaction key (first of brq_transactions)
information_flows: depends: payment (inherits the provider/transaction engine + redirect-form rendering + _process state machine)

outbound (redirect): _get_specific_rendering_values -> signed hidden-field POST form -> browser auto-submit to https://checkout.buckaroo.nl/html/ (sandbox testcheckout.buckaroo.nl) -- no server-to-server API call
inbound (return): Buckaroo -> POST /payment/buckaroo/return -> _normalize_data_keys -> _verify_signature (SHA-1 over raw data, constant-time compare) -> _process -> /payment/status
inbound (webhook/push): Buckaroo -> POST /payment/buckaroo/webhook -> _normalize_data_keys -> _verify_signature -> _process -> payment state machine
no tokenization / no refund / no capture / no void flows in this module
frontend_components: redirect_form QWeb template (payment_buckaroo_templates.xml; server-rendered hidden-field auto-POST form to the Buckaroo HTML gateway; no JS/OWL)

external_integrations.sdk: none (no python SDK and no browser SDK; card/iDEAL/wallet data entered on Buckaroo's hosted HTML gateway, never in Odoo)
external_integrations.auth: no transport bearer token; the pre-shared buckaroo_secret_key is used ONLY to compute/verify the SHA-1 signature (Brq_signature outgoing, brq_signature incoming) over the prefix-filtered, lowercase-sorted key=value payload
external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: a real external acquirer integration in its hosted-redirect form. Although uses_api_keys=true, there is NO authenticated S2S endpoint -- the secret key is purely a signing pre-shared secret. The browser POSTs a server-signed hidden-field form to Buckaroo's BPE HTML gateway (live or sandbox by provider.state), the buyer pays on Buckaroo, and Buckaroo returns the signed feedback to /payment/buckaroo/return and pushes to /payment/buckaroo/webhook, both verified by recomputing the SHA-1 signature. The base 'payment' engine ships no live acquirer; this module is that override, contrasting with Stripe/Xendit by being redirect-only (no S2S API, no tokenization).
external_integrations.note: Gap-#7 example where uses_api_keys=true is misleading: the 'key' is a signing secret, not a transport credential. None of the Buckaroo HTML-gateway endpoints, the prefix-filtered SHA-1 signing, or the numeric BRQ_STATUSCODE->state mapping are derivable from Python model/field metadata; they were established only by reading const.py + payment_provider.py + payment_transaction.py + controllers/main.py.

capabilities: Accept Card and iDEAL payments via Buckaroo's hosted HTML gateway across the Netherlands and Europe
Accept European local payment methods (iDEAL, Bancontact, Belfius, KBC, SOFORT, Przelewy24, EPS, Trustly, Klarna, in3, SEPA Direct Debit, PayPal, ...) mapped to Buckaroo service names
Signed-redirect settlement (SHA-1 over prefix-filtered payload + secret key) with no card data in Odoo
Multi-currency acceptance bounded to Buckaroo's 8 supported currencies (EUR/GBP/PLN/DKK/NOK/SEK/CHF/USD)
value_streams: Collect-Payment (redirect): initiate tx -> _get_specific_rendering_values builds the signed BPE form -> browser auto-POST to the Buckaroo HTML gateway -> buyer pays on Buckaroo -> POST /payment/buckaroo/return (signature-verified) AND/OR async push POST /payment/buckaroo/webhook -> _process -> state machine pending/done/cancel/error
Settle: BRQ_STATUSCODE 190 -> _set_done -> downstream post-process settlement (account_payment / sale)
information_concepts: payment.provider (Buckaroo credentials: website key, secret key)
payment.transaction (mapped to a Buckaroo BPE order; keyed by brq_invoicenumber=reference, provider_reference=first brq_transactions key)
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; buckaroo_secret_key is restricted to base.group_system; the website key and everything else inherit payment's groups/record rules)
policies: Inbound authenticity: return and webhook data must pass _verify_signature (SHA-1 over the prefix-filtered, lowercase-sorted payload + secret key, constant-time hmac.compare_digest) or are rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden
Outbound redirect-form integrity: the form is signed into Brq_signature before the browser POSTs it to Buckaroo
Signature scope is restricted to keys prefixed add_/brq_/cust_ (case-insensitive); the brq_signature key itself is excluded and values URL-decoded on incoming
Supported currencies bounded to const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES (EUR/GBP/PLN/DKK/NOK/SEK/CHF/USD); others filtered out by _get_supported_currencies
All four result URLs (return/cancel/error/reject) are sent and signed even though they share one value
Secret key gated by base.group_system field group
stakeholders: Merchant / Company (res.company, holds the Buckaroo website key & secret key)
Buckaroo (external acquirer / PSP, Netherlands, covering several European countries)
Accountant (consumes settled payments via account_payment downstream)
metrics: (no own reports; transaction volumes/amounts/state surfaced by the parent payment.transaction pivot/graph)

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_buckaroo is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter whose purpose is to interconnect two parties who would not otherwise transact directly -- the European cardholder/iDEAL user and the merchant -- by linking the merchant to Buckaroo's payment network. It exhibits the mediating-technology activities: network promotion & contract management (website key + signing secret-key management, per-method and supported-currency enablement), service provisioning (building and signing the per-transaction BPE redirect and confirming the signed return/push feedback), and infrastructure operation (the hosted-redirect handoff to the Buckaroo HTML gateway plus the signature-verified return/webhook settlement loop). It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's value_model exactly: the engine is the generic mediator and this module is its Buckaroo realization. activity_class is 'support' because, from the enterprise value-chain perspective, payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False, no end-user app) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash, with the side of 'manage an external payment provider'. So value_model=network (its own internal logic is mediation, an acquirer integration -- gap #7), activity_class=support (its place on the enterprise value chain). This mirrors the sibling payment_stripe / payment_xendit metamodels (network/support) and the parent payment engine; like APS and AsiaPay, Buckaroo is a redirect-only acquirer (no S2S API, no tokenization), here with a fuller pending/done/cancel/refused/error status model and a SHA-1 prefix-filtered signature.

standard_capabilities: hosted-redirect payment via the Buckaroo BPE HTML gateway (live checkout.buckaroo.nl vs sandbox testcheckout.buckaroo.nl by provider.state)
European local payment-method routing (iDEAL / Bancontact / Belfius / KBC / SOFORT / Przelewy24 / EPS / Trustly / Klarna / in3 / SEPA Direct Debit / PayPal / ... mapped to Buckaroo service names)
signed-redirect integrity and signature-verified settlement via a SHA-1 hash over the prefix-filtered payload + secret key
asynchronous settlement via a signature-verified push webhook plus an (also signature-verified, POST) redirect-return route
typical_fits: online shop / portal checkout collecting card or iDEAL/European-method payments through Buckaroo
send-a-payment-link or pay-an-invoice-online collection (with account_payment / sale downstream)
merchants needing card/iDEAL acceptance without holding card data (Buckaroo-hosted gateway, nothing entered in Odoo)
Benelux / European checkouts dominated by iDEAL, Bancontact, SOFORT, Klarna and SEPA Direct Debit
common_gaps: no server-to-server API: only the hosted-redirect BPE flow is implemented (no direct/S2S charge, no inline form); the 'secret key' is a signing secret, not a transport credential
no tokenization / saved cards (no _extract_token_values, no off-session recurring) -- every payment is a fresh redirect
no manual capture / authorize-then-capture, no void, and no in-module refund operation

signature pinned to SHA-1 (not configurable); the public-URL requirement for the return/push means local/dev instances need a tunnel; without the secret key set, verification has no secret to compare against
currency support bounded to const.SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES (8 currencies); other currencies are filtered out
bespoke reconciliation / settlement document chains live downstream (account_payment, sale), not here

curl -X POST https://<host>/payment/buckaroo/webhook (csrf=False, auth=public) with a missing/invalid 'brq_signature' field -> expect HTTP 403 Forbidden from _verify_signature

open_questions: Exact Buckaroo BPE gateway request and push/return field sets beyond those built in _get_specific_rendering_values / read in _apply_updates (brq_invoicenumber, brq_amount, brq_currency, brq_transactions, brq_payment_method, brq_statuscode, brq_signature).
Real-world distribution of Buckaroo transaction states (pending/done/cancel/refused/error) and method mix (card vs iDEAL vs other European methods) -- no runtime row counts captured.
How refunds / chargebacks are handled operationally given no in-module refund override (likely via the Buckaroo Plaza dashboard or a downstream module).
Whether instances reliably register the push webhook vs rely on the (also signed) POST return route, and whether both can fire for the same transaction.
